content:
iPadOS and macOS were two very different software platforms in the past. However, especially since iPadOS 26, the two have become increasingly similar. This year the trend is even more pronounced, as iPadOS 27 adds three features that make the iPad more like a Mac.

#1: Status bar shows app name

The one I use daily is an M5 iPad Pro that stays connected to a Magic Keyboard most of the time. And the iPad has always had an issue for keyboard users — the lack of a clear "current app" indicator.

If there is only one app on screen, that is no problem. But if you can see several apps at once, using keyboard shortcuts becomes very troublesome. I cannot count how many times I thought a shortcut would be triggered in one app, only to find it actually fired in another.

Mac actually solved this problem long ago by showing the name of the current app in the top-left corner of the screen. iPadOS 27 can now do the same.

iPadOS 27 users will find the name of the current app displayed in the status bar, alongside information such as the time and date. Although it is a small change, it makes the experience of operating an iPad with a keyboard far more comfortable.

#2: Permanently display the menu bar

Another welcome change in iPadOS 27 is the option to keep the menu bar permanently displayed.

Apple first brought the menu bar to the iPad last year. But unlike on the Mac, the menu bar in iPadOS 26 only appeared when the user actively summoned it.

In iPadOS 27, the Settings app has added a new toggle under "Multitasking & Gestures" labelled "Auto-show and hide menu bar".

Once you turn this option off, the menu bar stays visible at all times. I have been using it this way during the iPadOS beta period, and I would say it is one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Everyday operations at Mac-level speed

Although I love my iPad and am very grateful for its new capabilities in iPadOS 26 and 27, I do sometimes get frustrated by how slow some basic operations are. For example, I wrote earlier this year: "Right-clicking in iPadOS often feels sluggish and stuttery, whereas on the Mac it is instantaneous."

Thanks to Apple's focus this year on fixing bugs, I am happy to say that iPadOS 27 has improved the speed of these kinds of everyday operations.

Apple says right-clicking with the mouse cursor to open the context menu is now faster, and I can clearly feel it myself. Browsing files and transferring them to an external drive is now "up to 5 times faster" — Apple says this is now as fast as Finder on the Mac. App launches are more responsive, and window-management actions such as closing, switching or dragging windows are also faster.

There are still areas where the Mac is faster and the iPad can feel sluggish. But overall, the speed improvements in iPadOS 27 are a major step in the right direction.

What are your favourite new features and changes in iPadOS 27? Let us know in the comments section.
